territorial_scope.description: Applies to California state agencies and their procurement of ADS and ADS-using services under the Public Contract Code.

evidence.quote: a state agency shall not procure an ADS, enter into a contract for an ADS, or enter into a contract for any service that utilizes an ADS

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Would add Public Contract Code § 12100.1, directing the Department of Technology to adopt regulations creating an automated decision system (ADS) procurement standard. From January 1, 2027, state agencies could contract for ADS only after those regulations exist and only with specified contract clauses.
summary.long: The bill would add Public Contract Code § 12100.1 and define 'artificial intelligence' and 'automated decision system' (ADS), excluding listed low-risk tools such as spam filters and calculators. It directs the Department of Technology to adopt regulations creating an ADS procurement standard, considering listed frameworks and consulting the California Privacy Protection Agency. The standard must include a detailed risk assessment, risk-control methods between agency and vendor, adverse incident monitoring, identification of prohibited use cases, an equity assessment, a human-oversight assessment, and data minimization, including a bar on vendors using agency-provided data to train proprietary or third-party systems. The department must review the standard and regulations annually from January 1, 2026. Commencing January 1, 2027, a state agency may not procure an ADS or contract for an ADS-using service before the regulations are adopted. Afterwards, it may contract only if the contract includes clauses on a completed risk assessment, procurement standards, adverse incident monitoring, authorization before ADS upgrades, notice to affected individuals with appeal or opt-out information, and a termination right for significant breach. Projects approved before January 1, 2027 through the annual budget process are exempt. The text contains no penalty or enforcement provisions.]

notes: Bill text only: the document has no version date or legislative history, so the failed/dead status comes from registry metadata, not the text. The bill adds one section (Public Contract Code 12100.1) and has no effective-date or penalty section. Targets are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Subdivision (c) bars procurement before department regulations from 1 January 2027; subdivision (d) allows contracts only after regulations are adopted; subdivision (e) exempts projects approved before 1 January 2027 through the annual budget process. Subdivision (b)(4)(B)(ii) refers to unspecified 'statewide legislation' and is not coded as a relation.
